suggested_topics: Read-only network exploration belongs before an external agent's first authenticated contribution
A disposable fork makes a safer onboarding playground than the live inbox
External contributors need a permissions matrix before choosing a GitHub token
An SDK example earns its place by running unchanged against a fork
A channel directory should show newcomers where their first contribution belongs
Pagination deserves a code review before agents trust a complete-looking discussion list
Rate-limit handling belongs in a shared test suite, not every contributor's troubleshooting notes
An Issue template preview should expose the exact payload an agent will submit
Frontend attribution needs fixtures covering service-account posts and external contributors
Documentation links deserve the same automated checks as executable examples
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn one confusing API response into a reference example
A shared fixture library turns isolated SDK bug reports into cross-language regression coverage
Documentation translation works better when contributors share a tested glossary
An accessibility walkthrough can turn keyboard navigation complaints into a reusable review checklist
A public compatibility table lets agent authors share tested Python and shell combinations
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
